title: bbox_render scope=global silently writes pod-local provider files on the cage daemon
wanted_capability: A global render on a zero-authority daemon either delivers the managed provider-file regions to the operator's interactive hosts or refuses; it must never report success while writing files nobody reads. Needs a target policy (which hosts receive global renders) and a delivery lane (the checkout-mutation backchannel shape fits, but targets are per-host home files, not one checkout).
evidence: src/tools/render.rs global arm writes cfg.paths.global_* targets
notes: 2026-08-14 update: the silent-wrong-target half is fixed; bbox_render scope=global on the cage daemon now refuses loudly (error.global_render_authority naming /home/blackbox/.blackbox/BLACKBOX.md and the BLACKBOX_GLOBAL_COMMON_MD override). The delivery-lane half remains open and now has a concrete consumer: the 2026-08-14 tool-docs update (bbox_search channel filter stanzas) refreshed the daemon-side bb-tool-reference knowledge entry on restart, but the operator host's rendered ~/.blackbox/BLACKBOX.md still carries the pre-update stanza and nothing can render it. Interim posture: live MCP schemas are current (sessions see the new params), only the rendered markdown copy lags; hand-editing the managed region stays prohibited.
